modules.module_title: Introduction to DCI Evaluator and Components of DCI

pcs.pc_description: Identify the key responsibilities and functions of a Digital Connectivity Infrastructure (DCI) Evaluator and how they contribute to the implementation and maintenance of digital services.
Evaluate how effective digital infrastructure evaluation supports broader national development goals, including economic growth, urban planning, and technological advancement.
Recognize and describe various elements of smart city infrastructure such as Smart Poles, public Wi-Fi kiosks, and electric vehicle (EV) charging stations.

Engage with or explain the roles of key players such as the Digital Connectivity Rating Agency (DCRA), Property Managers, Telecom Service Providers (TSPs), and Digital Connectivity Infrastructure Providers (DCIPs) in digital infrastructure deployment.
Carry out tasks associated with evaluating and assessing digital connectivity infrastructure according to established standards and guidelines.
Construct or interpret visual representations of DCI components, including sample layouts, system diagrams, and architectural models.
Develop or analyze basic infrastructure designs and network topologies that support digital connectivity in urban environments.

modules.module_title: Regulations, Standards and Permissions

pcs.pc_description: Demonstrate knowledge of the roles and responsibilities of TRAI, DoT, and BIS in setting policies, regulations, and standards for telecom and digital connectivity infrastructure.
Locate and implement applicable standards such as BIS structured cabling norms and DoT guidelines for telecom tower setup and fiber optic deployment.
Analyze central and state-level RoW regulations related to laying underground and overhead telecom infrastructure and apply them in real-world planning scenarios.
Determine the necessary licenses and compliance categories required for deploying digital connectivity infrastructure in line with regulatory requirements.
Verify that digital infrastructure projects meet the Model Building Bye Laws (MBBL) and National Building Code (NBC) standards.
Use national and international benchmarks, including Smart City norms, to assess the preparedness of urban areas for digital connectivity solutions.
Read and explain sample documents such as TRAI recommendations and DoT circulars to understand their implications on DCI planning and execution.
Illustrate and interpret annexures like site layouts, route maps, NOC requests, and safety certifications required during infrastructure deployment.
Create and maintain digital records, select routes using mapping tools, and track approval processes involved in DCI implementation.

modules.module_title: Digital connectivity Registration process and Rating Lifecycle

pcs.pc_description: Assess whether an individual or organization meets the required qualifications and prerequisites for registering with the Digital Connectivity Rating Agency (DCRA).
Carry out the steps involved in submitting a registration application to the DCRA, including document preparation and submission procedures.
Follow the process through which registration is approved and how registered entities are listed on the official digital connectivity rating platform.
Adhere to the terms and requirements specified by regulatory authorities for maintaining valid DCRA registration.
How to perform all duties and responsibilities expected from a registered Digital Connectivity Rating Agency as per regulatory guidelines.
Execute the registration process for Property Managers under the digital connectivity rating framework, including submission of necessary forms and documents.
Fulfill the roles and obligations assigned to Property Managers regarding digital infrastructure compliance and property readiness for rating.
Categorize buildings or developments into appropriate classes according to their type and intended use for digital connectivity evaluation.
Apply the established methodology to evaluate and rate a property’s digital connectivity infrastructure based on defined benchmarks.

Fill out mock or sample registration forms for DCRA or Property Manager registration, identifying and attaching all required documentation.

modules.module_title: Understand the elements of Active and Passive Infrastructure

pcs.pc_description: Understand the roles of active (e.g., routers, switches, access points) and passive (e.g., cables, patch panels, connectors) network infrastructure.
Explain how these components interact to enable seamless network communication, adhering to relevant industry standards and protocols.
Understand the set up and configure active network devices, such as routers and switches, to achieve desired network connectivity and functionality.

How to accurately terminate test passive network components, including cables and connectors, performing comprehensive continuity and performance tests on cabling systems to ensure proper data transmission.
Understand how to effectively integrate active network components with existing passive infrastructure, ensuring all parts work together as a cohesive system.
How to systematically inspect both active and passive network systems to identify and resolve potential faults, maintaining overall system integrity and performance.

modules.module_title: Prior processing for DCI

pcs.pc_description: How to accurately assess the physical environment, including dimensions, layout, ventilation, and power, to determine optimal equipment placement and cable routing. This includes identifying potential obstructions or interference and creating detailed floor plans that designate equipment installation areas.
How to develop network topology diagrams that visualize device connectivity. Select appropriate cabling types (e.g., Ethernet, fiber optics) and specify routing paths.
Accurately estimate quantities of all necessary cables, connectors, and hardware components, ensuring adherence to TIA/EIA and ISO/IEC standards.

Identify to verify the quality of all cables, connectors, and hardware components before installation. This also involves pre-configuring network equipment (routers, switches, access points) with initial settings like default IPs and passwords, and cutting and labeling cables for efficient identification.
Understand the cable cutting and labeling practices and explain correct crimping of RJ45 connectors test cables for continuity to ensure reliable connections.
Understand the redundancy and failover mechanisms to ensure uninterrupted connectivity.
How to set up default IPs, passwords, and initial configurations for all routers, switches, and access points prior to deployment.

modules.module_title: Basics of Drone Landing at Digital Infrastructure

pcs.pc_description: Understand correct safe drone landing techniques, ensuring proper altitude control, controlled descent speed, and accurate landing zone selection.
Explain how to apply awareness of site-specific conditions within digital connectivity infrastructure (e.g., Data center rooftops, fiber cable zones) to adjust landing approach.
Understand how to Assess environmental conditions wind speed, visibility, GPS signals quality and surface stability before commencing landing.
Discuss how to implement precautionary measures to minimize electromagnetic interference (EMI) and safeguard network hardware or communication lines.
Understand how to respond effectively to operational challenges such as signal loss, sensor malfunctions, or obstacle detection alerts during descent.
Understand DGCA regulations and site-specific standard operating procedures while executing drone landing.
